question.text: Nanda Patil runs 'Sahyadri Mid-Market PE' (Cat II). Her thesis: acquire minority stakes in growing profitable businesses (30%+ revenue growth, single-digit EBITDA margin) and help them scale. Per Chapter 9, this is best labelled as:

answer.text: Venture Capital — since the companies are growing.

Growth Investing / Growth Equity — 'a common PE strategy wherein an investor acquires a minority stake, looking to further grow the company; typically at the intersection of VC and PE where companies are still growing but may have already shown some profitability'.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9: 'Growth investing is a common PE strategy, wherein an investor will acquire a minority stake, looking to further grow the company. These investments typically take place at the intersection of VC and PE, where companies are still growing but may have already shown some profitability.' The Trap: Option A misses the 'minority stake + profitability' combination. Option C is control (51%+) acquisition. Option D is for stressed companies, not growing ones. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covered growth-equity classification. XV uses it in sector notes. Manager's Pro-Tip: Growth equity deals often lack board control. Protect the fund with affirmative-vote clauses on key decisions (new debt, M&A, CEO exit, budget) even as a minority holder. Also negotiate a drag-along / tag-along symmetric pair in the SHA.
